property_summary: A call to newEmergencyOracle succeeds if and only if the caller is set as an admin before the call.
Any caller can successfully execute newEmergencyOracle on M, while only an admin can on P.
A caller without admin rights must have the call to newEmergencyOracle revert.

The owner of each deployed EmergencyOracle is always the msg.sender of newEmergencyOracle in the reference, but the buggy version deploys with owner=address(0), violating the invariant that there is no newEmergencyOracle call tracing to an oracle owned by address(0).
For any description input, the owner of the deployed EmergencyOracle returned by the newEmergencyOracle call must be msg.sender (the caller), but the bug sets it to address(0).
After any admin calls newEmergencyOracle, the owner of the newly deployed EmergencyOracle must equal that admin, but the bug sets it to address(0).

For any admin and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle(description) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event must contain an oracle address whose owner() equals the admin, but the bug deploys with owner=address(0).

For any given non-empty description string, the description() of the created EmergencyOracle must equal that description; the mutant always passes an empty string, so the oracle's description is always empty regardless of the input.

After a successful call to newEmergencyOracle(description), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event from C, containing the returned oracle address, must correspond to an EmergencyOracle whose description() matches that input argument; the mutant always passes empty string, so the oracle's description differs from any non-empty input given.

For any non-empty description string, the description of the EmergencyOracle deployed by newEmergencyOracle must equal the input description; the mutant always deploys with an empty description, so any call with a non-empty input violates this rule.
